tags.gist: Says the commenter's users cannot provide the complaints and reports that postmarket programs quietly treat as the first line of defense.
States the measurements' limits and recommends against any standard turning on developer intent, proposing only conditions observable without knowing why an output occurred.
Supports the trade in principle, with the comment addressing the condition it depends on and one device class for which it should not be available.
Says a reduction is a trade only if monitoring can detect what premarket evidence would have caught; grant it against demonstrated detection, never mere existence.
Reports a failure mode that resets at each session boundary, which periodic re-benchmarking cannot see and so should not justify any premarket reduction.
Says monitoring built on the device's self-report inherits its errors, so a reduction resting on it amounts to the device vouching for itself.
Would make the approach unavailable where users cannot self-verify, devices run offline, or harm is complete before detection can occur.
Argues the trade assumes monitoring can resolve the residual uncertainty; the measured GenAI failures never accumulate into a rate and reassessment erases them.
Reports within-session input loss that doubled between recordings and a session where presentation improved while false statements continued, offered without any rate.
Wants any reduction tied to a named failure mode and a detection demonstration showing the program surfaces it at a stated interval and sensitivity.
Wants the monitoring record independent of the device, a machine-produced access record against which the device's account is mechanically compared.
Describes the published open-source ledger, offered for any reviewer to apply to any device.
Wants a named recipient and notification interval for detected faults, shorter than the harm window; a caregiver at session end for users who cannot self-verify.
Bounds that recommendation: a named person learns of a device fault, with no surveillance or transmission of the user's communication.
Would exclude devices whose users cannot self-verify or report, since the feedback loop the trade relies on is absent by construction for them.
Would exclude disconnected operation, or require an on-device record that persists offline and reconciles later, since telemetry may never reach the sponsor.
Would make reversibility an explicit gate: no exchange where the credible harm cannot be reversed within the program's detection interval.
Would exclude single-user, long-duration deployments, where population signals are weak and averaging hides failures about one person.
Asks that the exchange be granted specifically, against demonstrated detection, an independent record and a named recipient, with four categories excluded.
Clarifies the measurements came from commercial assistants, establish occurrence not frequency, and separates verified instrument from policy argument.
Recommends against any standard turning on candour or intent, since every proposed condition can be observed without knowing why an output occurred.
Says a premarket reduction asks users to carry uncertainty personally, which is reasonable only for people who can see and report what happens to them.
